idiom_name: framework view function per route + explicit response object
implementation_notes: Python's idiom collapses ADR to one function per route: a Flask or Django view receives a parsed request, calls a domain function or service with plain arguments, and returns a response object (Flask's jsonify/Response, Django's HttpResponse/JsonResponse) - the function is the Action and the returned object is the Responder. The three-class structure is unnecessary while the format is uniform; keep a separate responder (or a Flask View subclass with dispatch_request) when one action must answer several representations or when response building is shared. Django class-based views are the same trade-off with a class instead of a function, and MethodView maps HTTP verbs to methods, which is per-verb rather than per-request and drifts toward Page Controller. FastAPI path operations are the same shape: def get_user(id: int) -> UserDto is the Action and the returned Pydantic model is the Responder.
pitfalls: Flask's request and g are context-local proxies: reading them inside Domain code silently couples business logic to the request context and breaks outside a request.
Passing an ORM entity directly to jsonify or a serializer either raises a type error or exposes fields and relationships according to serializer defaults; map to a plain dict or DTO in the Responder.
A Flask View with init_every_request = False is reused across requests: per-request state stored on self leaks across requests, so keep it on g or in local variables.
